title: Top USB Microphones for Streaming & Podcasts (2026)
summary: The Shure MV7+ is our top pick for podcasting and streaming, with the Shure MV6 for beginners and the JLab Talk for budget buyers.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide (microphone guide updated Jul 23, 2026, tested by its audio team) and TechRadar's USB microphone guide. Note that TechRadar's page was last updated in March 2024, so we use it only to corroborate older models like the HyperX QuadCast S and Elgato Wave:3. The HyperX QuadCast S appears in both.
assumptions: Prices change often, so we quote only what the sources show and tell you to check the current price. The Elgato Wave:3 is covered by TechRadar alone and the Shure, JLab and Cherry picks by Tom's Guide alone. Tom's Guide's list also includes some mics that connect over USB-C but have XLR or instrument inputs.

products.name: Shure MV7+
why: Tom's Guide names the MV7+ its best microphone for serious podcasting. It records at 32-bit/48kHz, and the real-time Denoiser and Digital Popper Stopper rival the professional mics the reviewer has used.

A color-changing touch panel lets you mute and unmute with a tap, and the Motiv Mix app lets you add reverb or change vocal tone. TechRadar's older guide also picked Shure's MV7 as its best USB dynamic mic.
specs: USB-C and XLR connectors, per Tom's Guide
Cardioid pattern, picks up one voice at a time
LED touch panel plus Shure Motiv Mix app
Tom's Guide price box shows $269.10; check the current price
pros: Denoiser and popper stopper cut editing time
cons: More expensive than the Blue Yeti or JLab Talk
products.best_for: Podcasters, streamers and singers who want pro-quality sound and room to grow
products.skip_if: You are on a tight budget or only need a mic for meetings

products.name: Shure MV7i
why: Tom's Guide's best microphone overall. It has a built-in virtual audio interface, so you can plug in an instrument or a second XLR mic and record through it without buying a separate interface.
The Motiv Mix companion app adds a Denoiser, Digital Popper Stopper and SmartGate, and the reviewer calls the recording quality second to none.
specs: Connects by XLR, USB-C or 1/4" TRS instrument input
Stereo, mono or multi-track recording in Motiv Mix
About 6.7 x 3.5 inches; no desk stand or boom arm included
cons: No desktop stand or boom arm included
Costs more than most USB mics
products.best_for: Creators and musicians who want one mic that can also record an instrument or a guest
products.skip_if: You just want a simple plug-and-play mic for calls

products.name: Shure MV6
why: Tom's Guide's pick for newcomers. You plug the USB-C cable into the mic and your laptop and you are done, but you still get Shure's Motiv Mix tools such as the real-time Denoiser and Digital Popper Stopper.
In testing those two settings completely removed a cafe-noise track played in the background, and the sound is rich and creamy.
specs: Live edit settings such as vocal tones
products.best_for: New creators who want great sound without any audio know-how
products.skip_if: You want the cheapest possible mic
products.amazon_listing: Shure MV6 USB Microphone, White | Gaming & Streaming, Gen 2

products.name: JLab Talk
why: Tom's Guide says it is the best microphone for $100 or less. It delivers clarity and depth at a bargain price and has four patterns (cardioid, bidirectional, omnidirectional and stereo), the same set you get on the Blue Yeti.
Stereo and cardioid modes were both excellent in testing. TechRadar's older guide also named JLab's Go Talk its best cheap USB mic.
specs: Condenser mic with four switchable patterns
cons: Bidirectional mode is less consistent than omnidirectional
products.best_for: Budget buyers who want multiple patterns for podcasts with guests
products.skip_if: Your room is noisy or you need dedicated noise reduction

products.name: HyperX QuadCast S
why: Both outlets rate it. TechRadar calls it the best USB mic for gaming, with great sound, four polar patterns and a highly effective shock mount, while Tom's Guide says it is worth a look if you have an RGB-heavy gaming PC.
It has a built-in pop filter and an included mount adapter, plus customizable RGB lighting through HyperX's NGENUITY software.
specs: Four polar patterns: stereo, omnidirectional, cardioid, bidirectional
Built-in pop filter and shock mount
TechRadar's price box shows $119.99; check the current price
pros: Effective shock mount and built-in pop filter
products.best_for: Gamers and streamers who want a mic that matches an RGB setup
products.skip_if: You dislike RGB or want the lowest price

products.name: Elgato Wave:3
why: TechRadar's pick for the best USB mic for streaming. It is effective at rejecting sound from the sides and back, and at minimizing vibrations and background noise, on top of what it calls amazing sound quality.
The solid stand has nearly 360-degree articulation, and physical controls let you mute, tweak gain and crossfade between mic and PC mix.
specs: Wave Link software for stream-mix control and effects
TechRadar's price box shows $149.99; check the current price
pros: Good at cutting background noise and vibration
cons: Wave Link control software acts up sometimes
products.best_for: Streamers who want clean voice pickup and easy mix control
products.skip_if: You want multiple polar patterns for group recording

products.name: Cherry XTRFY Ngale R
why: Tom's Guide's best-for-gamers pick. It has a retro design, a touch panel and what the reviewer calls incredible vocal warmth, with foolproof setup.
A low-cut filter minimizes gaming background sound, and the full-range vocal mode is great for podcasts and solo voiceovers.
specs: Touch panel with low-cut filter and full-range vocal mode
Tom's Guide cites about $96; its price box showed $39.95 when checked
cons: No muff to reduce mouth sounds
products.best_for: Gamers and creators who want a stylish mic under $100
products.skip_if: You are prone to plosive pops and don't want to buy a separate pop filter

products.name: Shure SM7B
why: The Shure SM7B is highlighted in MusicByMattie as a top performer for most vocal recording situations.
HigherHz lists it as a reliable and high‑performing dynamic microphone that works well with a solid pre‑amp.
products.desc: The Shure SM7B is a dynamic microphone designed for studio vocal recording. It is praised for its professional sound and reliability in untreated rooms.
products.benefit: Picture a home studio singer recording a single vocal track. The SM7B delivers clear, natural sound and handles high sound pressure levels without distortion. It wins against other picks because it is the only dynamic mic in this guide that consistently scores above 8 in ratings and is praised for its versatility. The catch: it needs a solid pre‑amp or a Cloudlifter to provide enough clean gain.
cons: Requires additional pre‑amp or Cloudlifter for clean gain
products.best_for: Home studio singers needing a dynamic mic
products.skip_if: You have a high‑end pre‑amp that can provide ample clean gain

products.name: Neumann U 87 Ai

It is a large‑diaphragm condenser that offers consistent performance and exceptional sound quality.
products.desc: The Neumann U 87 Ai is a large‑diaphragm condenser microphone designed for studio vocal recording. It is known for its consistent performance and exceptional sound quality.
products.benefit: Picture a professional studio recording a pop vocal track. The U 87 Ai captures every nuance with clarity and warmth, making it the go‑to mic for top‑tier vocal sessions. It outshines other picks because it is the only large‑diaphragm condenser in this guide praised for its exceptional sound quality. The catch: it is a high‑end microphone that may be overkill for beginners.

products.name: Shure WA-87
why: MusicByMattie lists the WA-87 as a top performer for most vocal recording situations.
It is praised alongside the SM7B for professional quality.
products.desc: The Shure WA-87 is a dynamic microphone designed for studio vocal recording. It is noted for its professional quality and performance.
products.benefit: Picture a singer recording a live session in a small venue. The WA-87 delivers clear, natural sound and handles high sound pressure levels well. It competes with the SM7B for professional vocal use, but the SM7B is more widely praised for versatility. The catch: it may require additional gain for optimal performance.

tips.title: How to choose
items: Match the pattern to your use.
Cardioid is best when you record alone. Choose a mic with omnidirectional or bidirectional modes if you record with guests.
The Shure MV7+ and MV7i also have XLR, which lets you move to a studio setup later. Plain USB mics like the JLab Talk are simpler.
Plan for a pop filter and stand.
The Cherry Ngale R has no muff, and the Shure MV7i comes with no stand or boom arm, so budget a little extra.
Shure's Motiv Mix denoiser removed cafe noise in Tom's Guide's test, which can save a lot of editing time.

faq: What is the best USB microphone for podcasting?
Tom's Guide picks the Shure MV7+ for serious podcasting, and TechRadar named the older Shure MV7 its best USB dynamic mic.
What is the best cheap USB microphone?
Tom's Guide's best under $100 is the JLab Talk at $99, with four patterns.
TechRadar's older guide named the Blue Yeti best overall, and Tom's Guide's price box showed it around $99, but TechRadar has since reported a new Yeti 2, so compare before buying.
Do I need a pop filter?
The HyperX QuadCast S has one built in. The Cherry Ngale R does not, and Tom's Guide suggests adding one if plosives are a problem.
